title: Tailorly Studio
summary: AI resume tailoring to the FAANG bar: rewrites your bullets to be quantified, system design aware and ATS safe, grounded in a base profile, then drafts the cover letter, outreach email and interview prep.

images.caption: The workspace: base profile with skill pills, target job panel and the get hire ready checklist.
Onboarding: upload an existing resume and the parser pre-fills every step, or start from blank.
Landing page: the promise, the numbers and the industries it is tuned for.
The full flow: paste a JD and watch the rest get drafted, step by step.

stories.title: Born from my own job hunt
stories.body: Tailorly came out of rewriting the same resume bullets over and over for different postings. The core bet never changed: a base profile keeps the AI grounded in your real experience, so nothing gets invented — just reframed to the bar.

stories.title: What I would do differently
stories.body: I would ship the ATS parser earlier and tighten it aggressively. The moment the model had clean, structured bullets to work from, every later step got easier.

title: Kiva
summary: The quoting and invoicing app for UK tradespeople. Speak a job out loud and AI writes a professional quote, then handles invoicing and getting paid.
role: Founder and sole full stack engineer

images.caption: Kiva landing page: speak a job, send a quote in seconds.

stories.title: The core loop already works
stories.body: Kiva is still in progress, but the heart of it is real: a tradesperson speaks the job out loud, FastAPI turns that into structured quote data, and React Native renders a professional quote in seconds — then invoicing and follow-ups take over.

stories.title: Why tradespeople first
stories.body: Quote-writing eats evenings. Most trades quote through WhatsApp or pen and paper, then chase payment one message at a time. Voice-first quoting meets them where the work happens, so the paperwork happens once instead of three times.

title: SimpleFin
summary: A full market research and portfolio workspace: live indices, watchlists, stock deep dives, benchmark comparisons and a personal dashboard, in one app.
role: Founder and sole full stack engineer

images.caption: Market overview: live indices, charts, the daily brief and market breadth at a glance.
Portfolio workspace: watchlists, holdings, simulation mode and asset allocation.
Stock deep dive: key statistics, financials, dividends, price history and simulation.
Benchmarks: any stock against the S&P 500 with beta, drawdown and correlation.
Sector performance and market movers, updated through the session.
Real traction, straight from Google Analytics.

stories.title: Two years, one pair of hands
stories.body: SimpleFin was my own venture and I built it full time for two years — every piece of it, from the market data layer to the dashboards. Watching 157K people show up on the analytics was the moment it stopped being a side thing and became a product.

stories.title: What I would do differently
stories.body: I would bring in the design system earlier. Retrofitting consistency across six major screens taught me a lot, but starting with a design system from day one would have been kinder to both the code and the users.

title: PXO Production Intelligence
summary: Production finance and planning intelligence for a global VFX studio: bid scenario worksheets, planning networks, portfolio dashboards and document pipelines, in six currencies and four languages.
ownershipText: Built for Pixomondo: production finance workspace, in-role

images.caption: Bid planning: a network of weekly bids, versions and the active path, over an editable timeline.
Bid worksheet: 180 shots at once with facility, per-discipline day rates and multi-currency totals.
Portfolio dashboard: revenue by studio, cost breakdown and margin by project across regions.
Settings: four languages and six currencies, with live number formatting.
Document management: EFC workbooks wired to bid files for reconciliation.

stories.title: The workflow before this
stories.body: Bids, forecasts and status reports used to live in separate workbooks. PXO pulls them into one place: bid versions over an editable planning timeline, worksheet scenarios you can duplicate and compare, and dashboards that roll everything up studio by studio.

stories.title: The hardest part
stories.body: The worksheet. Doing spreadsheet-grade UX for 180 shots with per-discipline day rates, multi-currency totals and four languages, all without a single number drifting, was the deep end of this build.

stackNotes.reason: The whole workspace is four screens of dense, composable UI (worksheets, networks, dashboards, settings) that all share state. React component model keeps that manageable while the ecosystem covers graphs and charts.

Bid planning is a live node graph: weekly bid versions as nodes, dependencies as edges, and one active path highlighted. React Flow gives zoom, selection and edges out of the box instead of hand-rolling SVG by shot count.

Production finance lives in spreadsheets. Planners think in rows, filters and totals, so the bid worksheet speaks that language: 180 shots, per-discipline day rates, formulas-in-place and scenario copies — with zero retraining.
The studio runs across regions, so numbers have to survive translation: labels, dates and currency formatting localize across four languages without a single total drifting.
